CVE-2024-11407.description: There exists a denial of service through Data corruption in gRPC-C++ - gRPC-C++ servers with transmit zero copy enabled through the channel arg GRPC_ARG_TCP_TX_ZEROCOPY_ENABLED can experience data corruption issues. The data sent by the application may be corrupted before transmission over the network thus leading the receiver to receive an incorrect set of bytes causing RPC requests to fail. We recommend upgrading past commit e9046b2bbebc0cb7f5dc42008f807f6c7e98e791

GHSA-p3vr-xp4c-r8fh.title: gRPC Ruby: bundled CA store trusts compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs
GHSA-p3vr-xp4c-r8fh.description: ### Summary gRPC Ruby (the [grpc](https://rubygems.org/gems/grpc) gem) verifies TLS connections against its bundled root certificate store (`roots.pem`) by default. In affected versions, this store trusts certificates issued by eight eMudhra intermediate CAs whose private keys are [compromised](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/). These intermediates have been revoked, but they still chain to the bundled `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root. An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue certificates for any hostname, and gRPC Ruby accepts them. An attacker who also has an on-path position can intercept or modify gRPC traffic. Upgrade to the patched version for your release line, or to 1.84.1 or later. ### Details The bundled store is separate from the operating system's trust store. On its own, updating the OS store (for example, `ca-certificates`) doesn't affect it. gRPC doesn't check certificate revocation (CRL/OCSP) by default, so revoking the intermediates doesn't mitigate the issue. gRPC also doesn't enforce Certificate Transparency, so it accepts certificates that were never publicly logged. Sectigo's `AAA Certificate Services` has also cross-signed the compromised intermediates. Older gRPC Ruby releases bundle that root as well, so they're affected even if they predate the emSign root. The patched releases trust neither root. ### Workarounds If you can't upgrade the `grpc` gem, first make sure the system CA bundle is up to date. For example, on Debian 13 (trixie), update the `ca-certificates` package to `20250419+deb13u1` or later ([DSA-6572-1](https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/DSA-6572-1)). Then point gRPC Ruby at that bundle by setting the `GRPC_DEFAULT_SSL_ROOTS_FILE_PATH` environment variable before starting your application. On Debian, that bundle is at `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`: ```sh export GRPC_DEFAULT_SSL_ROOTS_FILE_PATH='/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt' ``` gRPC Ruby then uses this file instead of its bundled roots. If the file is missing or unreadable, gRPC Ruby logs an error and falls back to the bundled roots. ### References - https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/ - https://groups.google.com/a/mozilla.org/g/dev-security-policy/c/0R3XLJL6FuE/m/0XofdebrAAAJ - [GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2) (certifi) - https://github.com/grpc/grpc/commit/8b32af3bf498c2ba9667410eaa8c836e700e97e6 (fix) - [GHSA-2xm2-c8xx-p9vh](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/security/advisories/GHSA-2xm2-c8xx-p9vh) (gRPC Python) - [GHSA-gvrc-7wf9-p7hg](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/security/advisories/GHSA-gvrc-7wf9-p7hg) (gRPC PHP) - [GHSA-mm89-g5jq-mmfq](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/security/advisories/GHSA-mm89-g5jq-mmfq) (gRPC Objective-C)
